dedupe_keys.name: cnnic statistical report on internet development in china semi annual and basic internet data

description: The Statistical Report on Internet Development in China is CNNIC's regular survey of the country's internet, published about twice a year since 1997; the 57th edition appeared on 5 February 2026 and the 56th on 21 July 2025. Each report gives national figures for internet users and mobile internet users, penetration in urban and rural areas, access devices, internet infrastructure (IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, domain names, websites, international bandwidth, mobile base stations and broadband ports drawn from ministry data) and use of online services, based on a telephone survey and data from operators and registries. CNNIC also publishes thematic reports, for example on generative AI applications and digital consumption, and its English site offers the reports, a Basic Data page with half-yearly headline indicators (for example 564 million internet users and 1,899,792 Mbps of international bandwidth at the end of 2012), an internet bandwidth map and a timeline. Coverage: mainland China. Format and access: PDF reports in Chinese, with English versions published later, free to read on the CNNIC websites. Caveats: headline figures are official estimates; methods and definitions have changed across editions, and English versions lag the Chinese releases. Simulation uses: demand and infrastructure context for studies of Chinese network capacity, international connectivity and exposure of users to outages. Related records: the MIIT green data centre list covers Chinese data centres, and the ITU indicators allow international comparison.
